sentences.text: Nebulasaurus is known only from a single fossil specimen, the holotype braincase labeled LDRC-v.d.1, which was in good state of preservation.
This dinosaur is distinguished by exoccipitals that nearly exclude the supraoccipital from the foramen magnum, which forms less than one-tenth of the margin.
The genus Nebulasaurus was described and named by Lida Xing, Tetsuto Miyashita, Philip J. Currie, Hailu You, and Zhiming Dong in 2015.
The name Nebulasaurus means "misty cloud lizard," combining the Latin word for misty cloud with the Greek word for lizard to reference the meaning of Yunnan.
The Zhanghe Formation contains a diverse fauna including the basal sauropodomorph Yunnanosaurus youngi and two other basal eusauropods.
The diverse sauropodomorph fauna of the Middle Jurassic in Asia preceded the dominance of mamenchisaurids seen in East Asia during the Late Jurassic.
Phylogenetic analysis identifies Nebulasaurus as a sister taxon to the African dinosaur Spinophorosaurus.
Nebulasaurus is classified as a basal eusauropod, though its braincase resembles those of more advanced neosauropods.
Nebulasaurus lived during the early Middle Jurassic in the Zhanghe Formation of Yunnan Province, China.
The fossil was found in terrestrial sediments deposited between 174 and 168 million years ago during the Aalenian and Bajocian stages.
